reason: The plan draws only the fort wall (short exposed segments in trenches and a dashed conjectured outline), the excavation trenches and the site grid. None of these could be identified with confidence in eight imagery releases: the trenches are backfilled or overgrown, no exposed wall segment is visible, the mound's edges are hidden under a tree belt on the north-west and east sides and under scrub elsewhere, and the plan draws no road, building, well or other modern feature.

candidates_considered.feature: exposed fort-wall segments in trenches (north corner, north-east arm, eastern and south-eastern trenches, western arm near the shrine)
candidates_considered.why: no stone wall line visible in any release; a straight pale line along the inner edge of the eastern tree belt (2021-22 release 16749) has the same general run as the north-east arm but no defined ends and could equally be a path or field edge

candidates_considered.feature: north corner of the fort, exposed in the trench complex at grid X-BB 11-19
candidates_considered.why: the apex where the north-west and eastern tree belts meet is the nearest candidate, but the belts follow the nala and field edges and the corner itself lies under trees

candidates_considered.feature: dashed conjectured outline of the fort (east, south and west corners), as a proxy for the mound edge
candidates_considered.why: conjectured, not surveyed; the mound edge is not visible as a sharp break in the imagery, and the vegetation boundaries that might mark it (tree belts, the edge of the dark scrub to the south-west) do not form a figure of the plan's size and shape

candidates_considered.feature: excavation trenches (blue outlines and grey-filled excavated areas)
candidates_considered.why: no rectilinear cuts or spoil heaps matching the trench layout in any release; a pale cleared patch on the west-central mound top in releases 8432 and 16749 does not match any trench outline in size or shape

candidates_considered.feature: site grid (letters J-NN, numbers 10-42) and north arrow
candidates_considered.why: survey grid with no surviving pegs visible

candidates_considered.feature: modern Hanuman shrine on the western arm (named in the text, p. 362)
candidates_considered.why: a small white building is visible on the west part of the mound in all releases, but the plan does not draw it; it was used only to confirm the location

notes: The site was located from the UTM ticks of the paper's digital elevation model (Fig. 2, about 690400 E, 2591050 N, read as UTM zone 42N, i.e. about 23.4182 N, 70.8635 E), which agree with the plans-v1 coordinate (23.4179 N, 70.8634 E), and from the modern shrine on the mound's west side described in the text. The mound lies between a tree belt along the nala to the north-west, a tree belt to the east beside the road, and open grazing ground to the south-west. Zoom 19 is not available here (all tiles are placeholders). Releases 8432 and 16749 (2021-22) are offset by roughly 25-35 m from the later releases. Orientation statements seen: while reading the paper's text for the site description, we read on printed p. 361 that the fortification 'was not found along the cardinal directions' and is oriented NNW-SSE (with reference to Fig. 5), and on printed p. 360 that the houses were built 'at cardinal direction with the fort wall'. Both passages appeared in a text extraction of printed pp. 356-361 read for the site description.
